mainTopic: Where we learn women's exemption from time-bound positive מצוות (the היקש to תפילין), and the sources that women equal men in prohibitions, money cases and deaths.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא explained why women's exemption from time-bound positive מצוות is learned from תפילין and not from other cases. מצה and הקהל, and also תלמוד תורה and פרו ורבו, are each שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, and two such verses do not teach a general rule. Here the גמרא asks how this works for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who holds women are obligated in פרו ורבו. It answers that תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן are two verses that come as one, and it shows that פריה ורביה and מורא are each needed, so they are not such a pair. Then it asks about the view that two such verses DO teach. רבא sends us to the scholars of פפוניא, who turn out to be רב אחא בר יעקב. He compares the whole Torah to תפילין, so women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות and obligated in the rest. The גמרא defends this for רבי מאיר and for רבי יהודה, who holds there are three verses (מצה, שמחה, הקהל), and three verses never teach. Finally it turns to the משנה's rule on negative מצוות. It brings three sources that women equal men in punishments, money cases and deaths, and begins explaining why each one is needed. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What about the view that women must have children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the earlier answer works for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who holds the מצוה of פרו ורבו applies to women too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, who says the verse "And God blessed them… be fruitful and multiply" speaks about both men and women, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about one specific opinion. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds that women are obligated in פרו ורבו, so the earlier answer may not work for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the answer was that תלמוד תורה and פרו ורבו are two verses that come as one, so they teach no general exemption. If women are obligated in פרו ורבו, only תלמוד תורה is left as an exemption. So why not learn from it that women are exempt from every positive מצוה that is not time-bound?

keyTerms.meaning: "Be fruitful and multiply", the מצוה to have children
"What is there to say?", a way of asking how a view can explain something

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
who says: about both of them the verse says:
phrases.notes: "Both of them" means the man and the woman.

phrases.english: "And God blessed them… be fruitful and multiply"
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:28

phrases.english: what is there to say?
phrases.notes: In his view women must have children, so that מצוה can't count as one women are exempt from.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא, דְּאָמַר: עַל שְׁנֵיהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the earlier answer (from before this section) against the view of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, women are obligated in פרו ורבו, so תלמוד תורה seems to be the only positive מצוה that is not time-bound which women are exempt from. Why not learn from it that women are exempt from all such מצוות?

steps.title: Torah study and redeeming the firstborn are two verses that come as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, so they cannot teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach a rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Even for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, the two מצוות that are left still don't teach a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Torah states the same rule in two separate places, that shows the rule is special to those cases. If it were general, one verse would have been enough. So the women's exemption from תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן stays limited to those two מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses that teach the same thing
They do not teach a general rule for other cases
The מצוה to learn and teach Torah
Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: "Two verses that come as one" does not mean the verses are weak. It means that because the Torah repeated the rule, we see it applies only to these cases and not to everything else.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה וּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן
phrases.english: Because Torah study and the redemption of the firstborn son are
two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.
phrases.notes: If one verse could have taught it everywhere, the Torah wouldn't need two. So it's limited to these cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה וּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, so they don't teach a general exemption.

steps.title: Then having children and fearing parents should also be two verses that come as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, פריה ורביה and מורא (both מצוות women are obligated in) should also count as two verses that come as one and teach nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא too, פריה ורביה and fear of parents should be two verses that come as one, and they should not teach!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same tool against רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. Women are obligated in both of these מצוות even though neither is time-bound. So shouldn't they also be two verses that teach nothing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If that were true, the Torah would be saying twice that women are obligated, which would be wasted words. The גמרא will need to show that each verse teaches something the other could not.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of having children
Fear or awe of one's father and mother
Also, too

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka too,
let having children and fear [of parents] be
phrases.notes: Women are obligated in both of these, and neither one depends on a set time.

phrases.english: two verses that come as one
and not teach!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא נָמֵי, נִיהְווֹ פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וּמוֹרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the principle from step 2 to challenge רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא from a different angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא that the Torah gives women both פריה ורביה and מורא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both teach the same thing (women are obligated in a positive מצוה that is not time-bound), one of them looks unnecessary. That makes them שני כתובים הבאים כאחד.

steps.title: Both are needed: fear alone would not teach having children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers צריכי: if the Torah had written only מורא, we would have said women are exempt from פריה ורביה because the verse says "and conquer it", which fits men.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah had written only fear of parents and not having children, I would have said: the Torah said "and conquer it". A man, whose way is to conquer, yes; a woman, whose way is not to conquer, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It shows that each verse teaches something we could not learn from the other, starting with why פריה ורביה had to be written for women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that commands "be fruitful and multiply" ends with "and conquer it". Conquering is the way of men, so we might have thought the whole מצוה is only for men. Learning from מורא would not have been enough, so the Torah had to include women in פריה ורביה on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: They are both needed
"The Merciful One", meaning the Torah or ה׳
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
"And conquer it", the end of the פסוק of פרו ורבו

phrases.english: Both are needed,
for if the Merciful One had written fear [of parents],
and had not written having children,
I would have said:
"and conquer it," the Merciful One said,
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:28, the same פסוק as "be fruitful and multiply."

phrases.english: a man, whose way is to conquer: yes,
a woman, whose way is not to conquer: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each verse is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only מורא written, "and conquer it" would make us think פריה ורביה is only for men.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah had to include women in פריה ורביה on its own.

steps.title: Both are needed: having children alone would not teach fear of parents
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the צריכותא: if only פריה ורביה were written, we would have exempted women from מורא, since a married woman can't always do it, and so we would have exempted all women.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only having children and not fear of parents, I would have said: a man, who is able to do it, yes; a woman, who is not able to do it, no. And since she is not able to do it, she should not be obligated at all. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows why מורא also had to be written for women, so the two verses are not repeats and the challenge falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married woman's duties to her husband can stop her from serving her parents. So we might have exempted women from מורא. Since married women can't always do it, we might even have exempted every woman. Because each verse teaches something new, they are not שני כתובים הבאים כאחד.

keyTerms.meaning: It is in his power, he is able
At all
It is needed (closing the צריכותא)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, פריה ורביה and מורא are each needed, so they are not two verses that come as one. The only exemptions left are תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן, and those two ARE two verses that come as one, so they teach no general rule.

phrases.english: And if it had written having children

a man, who is able to do it: yes,

phrases.english: a woman, who is not able to do it: no,
phrases.notes: A married woman's duties to her husband may get in the way of serving her parents.

phrases.english: and since she is not able to do it
she should not be obligated at all,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וְלֹא כְּתַב מוֹרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer begun in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each verse is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only פריה ורביה written, a married woman's limits would have exempted all women from מורא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are needed, so פריה ורביה and מורא are not שני כתובים הבאים כאחד.

steps.title: But what about the view that two such verses do teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that this whole approach only works for the view that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד don't teach. For the view that they DO teach, the problem comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says two verses that come as one do not teach. But for the one who says they do teach, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new, bigger problem. All the answers so far depended on the rule that two such verses teach nothing, and not everyone holds that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For those who say two such verses DO teach, מצה and הקהל would teach that women are obligated in time-bound מצוות‎. תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן would teach that they are exempt from מצוות that are not time-bound. That is the opposite of the accepted rule, so why do we learn from תפילין instead?

keyTerms.meaning: "It is fine", meaning this works out for one view
According to the one who says
They do teach a general rule

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says

phrases.english: two verses that come as one do not teach,
but according to the one who says they do teach,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: Then מצה and הקהל, and תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן, would all teach rules, the opposite of what we hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the answers so far and shows they rest on one disputed rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole approach of using שני כתובים הבאים כאחד to explain why we learn from תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the view that such verses DO teach, the other verses would teach opposite rules about women, so the original question returns.

steps.title: רבא: the scholars of פפוניא know the reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the scholars of פפוניא know the reason for this. He does not spell it out himself; the next step gives it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The people of Pafunya know the reason for this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא responds to the question. He does not give an answer himself; he says the scholars of a place called פפוניא know it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא admits the question is real. He points to someone else's answer instead of giving his own. The next step names those scholars and gives their reasoning, so the question is answered there.

keyTerms.meaning: The people (scholars) of פפוניא, a place
Reason
Matter, thing

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not giving an answer here. He is saying an answer exists and is known to the scholars of פפוניא.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The people of Pafunya know it,
phrases.notes: פפוניא is a place. רבא means its scholars have the answer, and the next step tells us who they are.

phrases.english: the reason for this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: פַּפּוּנָאֵי יָדְעִי לַהּ לְטַעְמָא דְּהָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא points to the scholars of פפוניא as having the answer. Their reasoning, the היקש to תפילין, is given in the next step.

steps.title: Who the scholars of פפוניא are, and their comparison to תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The 'scholars of פפוניא' are רב אחא בר יעקב. He compares the whole Torah to תפילין, so women are exempt from every time-bound positive מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this? רב אחא בר יעקב. The verse says, 'And it shall be a sign on your hand and a remembrance between your eyes, so that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth.' The whole Torah is compared to תפילין. Just as תפילין is a time-bound positive מצוה and women are exempt, so too women are exempt from every time-bound positive מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the 'scholars of פפוניא' from Step 7. It then gives their source: a פסוק that links the whole Torah to תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about תפילין also mentions 'the Torah of ה׳', so the whole Torah is compared to תפילין. Women are exempt from תפילין, which is a time-bound positive מצוה. So the rule spreads to every time-bound positive מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: was compared (a היקש, linking two things in one פסוק so they share a rule)
the boxes with Torah passages worn on the arm and head
a positive מצוה caused by time, meaning it only applies at certain times
exempt (feminine plural)

phrases.english: And who is it? Rav Acha bar Yaakov:

phrases.english: Just as tefillin is a positive מצוה caused by time,
and women are exempt,

phrases.english: so too every positive מצוה caused by time:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the scholars רבא pointed to and gives their reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exemption of women from time-bound positive מצוות comes from comparing the whole Torah to תפילין.

steps.title: So women are obligated in מצוות that are not time-bound
steps.stepSummary: Since women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות, it follows that they are obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות, we can conclude that women are obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב finishes his teaching by drawing the flip side of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to תפילין only exempts women from time-bound מצוות. So we learn that in all other positive מצוות they are obligated. Because this היקש is a direct source for both rules, it outweighs anything מצה and הקהל, or תלמוד תורה and פדיון הבן, might teach. That answers the problem from Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: from the general statement, meaning 'it follows that'
obligated (feminine plural)
not caused by time; applies at all times

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the well-known rule about which positive מצוות women are obligated in.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּמִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ – נָשִׁים פְּטוּרוֹת,
phrases.english: And since from a positive מצוה caused by time, women are exempt,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּמִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ –
phrases.english: it follows that from a positive מצוה not caused by time,
women are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּמִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ – נָשִׁים פְּטוּרוֹת, מִכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the opposite side of the rule from Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות and obligated in those that are not time-bound. Both rules come from the היקש of the whole Torah to תפילין, which holds even for the view that two verses that come as one do teach.

steps.title: What about the view that תפילין is not time-bound?
steps.stepSummary: The comparison works only if תפילין is time-bound. The גמרא asks what to say for the view that תפילין applies at all times.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says תפילין is a time-bound positive מצוה. But for the one who says תפילין is not time-bound, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תפילין comparison. Some opinions hold that תפילין is worn at all times, so it is not time-bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תפילין is not time-bound, it cannot teach that women are exempt from time-bound מצוות. Then the problem returns: מצה and הקהל, where women are obligated, might teach that women are obligated in all time-bound מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: this works well
according to the one who says
what is there to say? (a challenge)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says

But for the one who says

phrases.english: tefillin is a positive מצוה not caused by time,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source just given in Steps 8 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the whole Torah to תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If תפילין is not time-bound, it cannot serve as the model for exempting women from time-bound מצוות.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: מצה and הקהל do not teach
steps.stepSummary: The view that תפילין is not time-bound belongs to רבי מאיר. He holds that מצה and הקהל are two verses that come as one, which do not teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who did you hear say that תפילין is not time-bound? רבי מאיר. He holds that these are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming the view: it is רבי מאיר. His other opinions solve the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that מצה and הקהל would teach that women are obligated in all time-bound מצוות‎. רבי מאיר holds that two verses teaching the same thing cannot be a model for other cases. So for him, those two cases stay limited to themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: whom did you hear say this?
two verses that come as one (teaching the same point)
they do not teach (to other cases)

phrases.english: Whom did you hear who says

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִילִּין מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ –
phrases.english: tefillin is a positive מצוה not caused by time?

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.
phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one do not teach.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the opinion and applying its other known rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without תפילין as a model, מצה and הקהל would obligate women in all time-bound מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, מצה and הקהל are two verses that come as one, so they teach nothing beyond themselves.

steps.title: What about רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה also holds that תפילין is not time-bound, but he says two verses that come as one do teach. So how does he avoid the problem?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה, who says two verses that come as one do teach, and also holds that תפילין is not time-bound, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same problem against another opinion that does not share רבי מאיר's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, תפילין cannot be the model, because he holds it is not time-bound. And מצה and הקהל should teach, because he holds two verses that come as one do teach. So it seems women should be obligated in all time-bound מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: they teach (a general rule)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
two verses that come as one do teach,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְפִילִּין מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ,
phrases.english: and tefillin is a positive מצוה not caused by time,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The answer of Step 11 does not work for רבי יהודה, so the challenge returns.
steps.kashyaTarget: How women are exempt from time-bound מצוות according to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He has neither escape: תפילין is not time-bound, and two verses that come as one do teach.

steps.title: Three verses that come as one never teach
steps.stepSummary: מצה, שמחה and הקהל are three verses teaching the same thing. Even רבי יהודה agrees that three such verses do not teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because מצה, rejoicing and הקהל are three verses that come as one, and three verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה by adding a third case where women are obligated in a time-bound מצוה‎: שמחה on the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three verses saying the same thing, the rule is stronger. Even those who say two such verses teach agree that three do not. So no general obligation for women in time-bound מצוות can be learned.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה to rejoice on the festival
the gathering of the whole nation to hear the Torah read, after the שמיטה year
three verses that come as one

steps.whatToRemember: Every opinion avoids learning from מצה and הקהל: either the היקש to תפילין, or the rule that two (or three) verses coming as one do not teach.

phrases.english: Because matzah, rejoicing and the assembly are
three verses that come as one,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁלֹשָׁה כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.
phrases.english: and three verses that come as one do not teach.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a third case that changes the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי יהודה, מצה and הקהל should teach that women are obligated in all time-bound מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Together with שמחה there are three verses, and three verses that come as one do not teach, even for רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Source for women in negative מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that women are obligated in all negative מצוות and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And all negative מצוות, etc.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה. It is setting up the next step, which will give the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that men and women alike are obligated in all prohibitions, time-bound or not. The גמרא now wants a פסוק for this.

keyTerms.meaning: a negative מצוה, a prohibition
from where are these words? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: "And all negative מצוות, etc."
From where are these matters known?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that women are obligated in all negative מצוות.

steps.title: A man or woman: equal in all punishments
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל, learn from 'a man or woman who commits any sin' that women equal men in all Torah punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: the verse says, 'A man or woman, when they commit any of the sins of man.' The verse made a woman equal to a man for all punishments in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source: a פסוק that mentions both man and woman together when speaking about sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק puts 'man or woman' side by side for any sin, women carry the same punishments as men. Punishment comes from breaking a prohibition, so women are bound by all negative מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: the school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל
the verse made equal
punishments

steps.whatToRemember: Women are equal to men in all prohibitions and punishments of the Torah, learned from 'a man or woman who commits any sin'.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and so taught the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
The verse states:
"A man or a woman, when they commit
any of the sins of man"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:6

phrases.english: the verse made a woman equal to a man
for all punishments in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'a man or woman who commits any sin' makes women equal to men for all punishments, so for all prohibitions.

steps.title: School of רבי אליעזר: women equal men in money cases
steps.stepSummary: From 'which you shall set before them', the school of רבי אליעזר learns that a woman is equal to a man in all money cases in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אליעזר taught: The verse says, 'which you shall set before them.' The Torah made a woman equal to a man for all the money laws in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source, from the school of רבי אליעזר. It shows that women are treated like men, this time in money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 covered punishments for sins. This source covers a new area: דינים, meaning money cases and damages. The word 'them' in the verse is understood to include both men and women.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי אליעזר
The verse made them equal
Money cases and damages laws

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Eliezer taught:
The verse says: "which you shall set before them"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:1, the opening of the money laws in פרשת משפטים.

phrases.english: The verse made a woman equal to a man
for all the judgments in the Torah.
phrases.notes: 'Judgments' here means money cases and damages, the topic of that פרשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source next to the one from step 15, covering money cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'them' in שמות 21:1 teaches that a woman is equal to a man in all money laws.

steps.title: School of חזקיה: women equal men regarding deaths
steps.stepSummary: From 'and killed a man or woman', the school of חזקיה learns that a woman is equal to a man for all deaths in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of חזקיה taught: The verse says, 'and it killed a man or a woman.' The Torah made a woman equal to a man for all deaths in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source, from the school of חזקיה. This one is about deaths caused by a person's animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is about an ox that kills a person, where the owner pays כופר (ransom). Because the verse says 'a man or a woman', the same law applies whether the victim was a man or a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of חזקיה
Deaths (here: deaths caused by one's animal)
And it killed

phrases.english: The school of Chizkiyah taught:
The verse says: "and it killed a man or a woman"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:29, about a dangerous ox that kills someone.

phrases.english: The verse made a woman equal to a man
for all the deaths in the Torah.
phrases.notes: He means that the ransom law applies whether the animal killed a man or a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third source, this time for deaths and the ransom (כופר).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'A man or a woman' in שמות 21:29 makes a woman equal to a man regarding deaths caused by one's animal.
steps.whatToRemember: Three sources, three topics: punishments for sins (step 15), money cases (רבי אליעזר), and deaths/כופר (חזקיה).

steps.title: Why the money source is needed beyond the first source
steps.stepSummary: All the sources are needed. From the first one alone, we might say the Torah gave women atonement out of pity, but money laws apply only to men, who do business.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are needed. If the Torah had taught only the first one, I would say the Merciful One had pity on her so she could get atonement. But for money laws I would say: a man, who does business, yes; a woman, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why it needs all three sources (צריכותא). It starts by showing that the first source could not teach us about money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first source (sins) could be explained by mercy: ה׳ wants a woman to be able to get כפרה too. Money laws come from a different reason, which is business, and we might think that is only a man's world. So a separate source is needed for money cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (each source is needed)
It taught us
Atonement
The Merciful One (ה׳) had pity
Business dealings

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying women really are left out of money law. It is only showing what we might have thought without the extra verse.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
phrases.notes: He means all the sources are needed. None of them is extra.

phrases.english: for if it had taught us only that first one,
phrases.notes: The 'first one' is the verse about sins from step 15.

phrases.english: because of atonement the Merciful One had pity on her,
but money cases, I would say:
a man, who does business dealings, yes,
a woman, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing three sources, the גמרא explains why the Torah needed each one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sins source alone could be explained by mercy for atonement, so it would not cover money laws. That is why the money-law source is needed.

steps.title: Why the ransom source is needed beyond the money source
steps.stepSummary: From the money source alone, we might say it applies to women because business can be their livelihood. But for ransom we might say otherwise. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us only this one (money laws), I would say that is because it can be her livelihood. But ransom, I would say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the צריכותא and starts showing why the money source cannot teach us about כופר. The sentence breaks off here and finishes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money laws apply to a woman because she may earn her living through business. כופר has nothing to do with livelihood, so we might think it does not apply to a woman. The גמרא is setting up exactly that thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Her livelihood
Ransom paid by the owner of an ox that killed a person
I would say (what we might have thought)

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only this one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the money-cases source from step 16.

phrases.english: I would say that is because it is her livelihood,
but ransom, I would say:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְועִינַן הָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּחַיּוּתַהּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second leg of the צריכותא, showing why the money source cannot cover כופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The money source could be explained by livelihood, which does not apply to כופר. The completion of this point comes next.
